name: Terminal Portfolio
focus: Grounded AI assistant and MCP server
tagline: This portfolio: a terminal-style site whose verified, source-cited knowledge base is also a public MCP server and the only source for its AI assistant.

overview.text: Alex's portfolio, built in TypeScript and Next.js around an interactive terminal. A structured knowledge base, in which every claim cites its sources, feeds the terminal, a public read-only MCP server with seven tools and four resources, and an AI assistant.

The assistant answers only from the portfolio's MCP tools and lists the sources under each answer. Every sentence is checked before it is shown: one whose figures don't appear in that turn's tool results is withheld.
Per-visitor rate limits and spending limits of $10 a day and $50 a month are checked before any model call; if they can't be checked, the request is refused.
Deployed on Vercel in October 2026 at www.builtbyaj.io.

responsibilities.text: Designed and directed the development of an AI-powered engineering portfolio, defining its requirements, architecture, security constraints and evaluation standards. Used Claude Code as an AI-assisted development tool, reviewing implementation decisions, testing behaviour and validating the results.

overview.text: Every claim in the knowledge base names its sources and is validated by a build step; claims marked unverified are kept out of everything public. The terminal and the MCP server read the same generated bundle, so there is no second copy of the data.
The MCP server has seven read-only tools and four resources, served over Streamable HTTP at /api/mcp (stateless, JSON responses) and over stdio.

The assistant's chat loop knows models only through one interface, with one adapter for the Claude API and Amazon Bedrock, and a scripted model for tests and local development. It calls the portfolio tools through an in-process MCP client, in at most four tool rounds per answer.

diagrams.title: How an answer is produced
diagrams.source:
flowchart LR
  terminal[Terminal in the browser] -- POST /api/chat --> route[Chat route: checks, rate limits, budget]
  route --> loop[Chat loop]
  loop -- tool calls --> mcp[In-process MCP client: portfolio tools]
  loop -- stream --> model[Claude API, Bedrock or scripted model]
  route -- checked sentences, server-sent events --> terminal

challenges.title: Keeping the assistant's figures grounded
challenges.problem: A language model can restate a figure wrongly or produce one that the portfolio doesn't contain.
approach: Every sentence is checked before it is shown: its figures must appear in that turn's tool results, or the sentence is withheld.
A sentence saying the portfolio doesn't record a project's section is withheld when that section has content but wasn't retrieved that turn.

challenges.title: Sharing a Redis database safely
challenges.problem: The rate limits and the AI budget use a Redis database that can be shared with other applications.
approach: Every portfolio key starts with `portfolio:`, and limiter names can't reach another namespace.
The portfolio only increments counters and sets their expiry; it never deletes, scans, renames or flushes keys, and a test checks this.

decisions.title: AI requests fail closed
decisions.decision: The chat route checks the request, the visitor's rate limits and a daily and monthly budget before any model call, and refuses the request if any of these checks can't be completed.
decisions.rationale: Every answer costs money, so an unavailable limit or budget store must not mean unlimited spending.
tradeoffs: If the store is down, the assistant is unavailable; the terminal's commands still work.

decisions.title: Choosing the model by evaluation
decisions.decision: Candidate models answer a fixed, versioned set of questions through the real chat endpoint, scored by deterministic rules, and every answer is reviewed by a person before any model change.
decisions.rationale: It makes the choice of model objective and repeatable, and catches what automated scoring misses.

lessons.text: Automated scores can miss things in both directions: a person reviewing the October 2026 evaluation found one unsupported claim the scorer had passed, and one correct answer it had failed.

limitations.text: As of October 2026 the AWS infrastructure for Bedrock hasn't been applied (the live assistant uses the Claude API directly), and only one candidate model has been evaluated.

undocumented: Usage figures (none recorded since it was deployed in October 2026)
